meeting_header:
Date: 2026-06-15 | Time: 14:00 UTC | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jared Kim (BrightBank Head of ML), Priya Desai (BrightBank Senior Infra), Liam O'Connor (BrightBank PM)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results vs BrightBank's current baseline provider. Redwood showed improved median latency and throughput in several configs; baseline has lower tail latency in one workload. Discussed tuning (batching, KV prefix caching, quantization) and security/network next steps. Agreed on additional runs and a 24h soak on Dedicated with caching enabled.
topics: Comparison vs baseline provider and possible sources of discrepancy
Tuning knobs: batching, prefix/KV cache, quantization profiles
Security/compliance items: SOC2, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, quick check-in we've got 45 minutes, I think. Carlos and I will run through the benchmark spreadsheet, then open for questions.
[00:12] Jared: Great, thanks. We have Priya and Liam here as well. Excited to see the numbers been comparing to BaselineCloud.
[00:20] Carlos: Cool. I'm Carlos, SE at Redwood. Quick note the spreadsheet link is in the chat: docs/benchmarks/brightbank-poc.csv, um, if anyone can't access ping me.
[00:35] Priya: I can open it, looks like you ran tests on the latest model variant and a quantized 4-bit profile?
[00:44] Carlos: Yes, so we ran three main configs: Hosted (standard), Dedicated GPU pool, and Dedicated with KV prefix caching + batching. For quant we used q4_0 profile which is our common perf config.
[00:58] Liam: Can you summarize the headline latencies?
[01:05] Carlos: Sure median token latency for typical 128-token prompts: Hosted ~ 42ms median, Dedicated ~ 36ms median, Dedicated + caching ~ 28ms median. For throughput, tokens/sec increased from ~1.1k on Hosted to ~1.6k on Dedicated+cache in our microbench.
[01:27] Jared: And how does that compare to our baseline provider? We saw median around 55ms last week.
[01:34] Carlos: Right, baseline median was 55ms in your tests. Our median improvements are consistent, but important caveat at the 95th/99th tail baseline was sometimes better on the long-ish sequence workload (prompt variability).
[01:49] Maya: This is important the tail behaviour seems to be workload dependent; in some cases their infra beats us because they have pre-warmed model shards for long contexts. We can replicate that with warm pools and slightly different batching policies.
[02:05] Priya: The 99th percentiles we saw on Dedicated without caching spiked to 650ms on longer sequences, which is concerning.
[02:14] Carlos: Yep that's where KV caching helped a lot. With prefix/KV cache enabled the 99th dropped to around 230ms in our test. I want to point out that the transcription here, sorry, the testbeds differ a bit BaselineCloud used mixed request sizes and a different concurrency distribution which hurts tail on our initial runs.
[02:37] Jared: Is there any mis-match in tokenization or model variant that could explain some of the difference?
[02:44] Carlos: We matched the model family and tokenizer, but their baseline was using a 16-bit float inference path on different GPU type which reduces variance on long sequences. Also they had a lower batch size by default so fewer queuing delays on certain sequence mixes.
[03:02] Priya: Can batching/queue knobs be tuned to improve our 99th without hurting median?
[03:10] Carlos: You can our suggestion is dynamic batching policy: smaller max batch for low-latency endpoints, adaptive queuing for bursts. Also enable KV prefix caching for repeated context patterns that yields the biggest tail wins for the same median.
[03:28] Liam: What about quantization tradeoffs any accuracy regression we should worry about?
[03:33] Carlos: For q4_0 we saw negligible quality delta on typical NLU tasks. We include quality evals in the sheet see evals tab but if you have a specific prompt set we can run regression tests.
[03:47] Jared: We will. Also security Priya had asked about KMS integration and audit logs.
[03:54] Maya: Yes we can provide SOC2 artifacts, KMS/HSM integration docs, and sample audit log export. I'll share a secure link after the call.
[04:05] Priya: For the private deployment: we'll need VPC peering, specific subnet ranges, and to confirm whether dedicated nodes can be placed in our tenancy.
[04:17] Carlos: We support VPC peering and private control plane; for Dedicated we can allocate customer-only GPU pools in the region. There was a minor note the on-prem package requires extra lead time.
[04:30] Jared: On the throughput numbers, can you run a 24h soak to measure variance over time? Our baseline provider had been stable but occasionally had long GC pauses.
[04:40] Carlos: Absolutely we can schedule a 24-hour soak on a Dedicated pool with prefix caching enabled and the same request mix. We'll need your OK to spin resources.
[04:50] Priya: We'll approve for a pilot, but need cost estimate.
[04:54] Maya: I'll include a pilot cost estimate in the pricing worksheet. Note: Dedicated pilot has a small discount.
[05:02] Jared: Why did baseline beat you on one of the longer-context tests is it kernel selection?
[05:08] Carlos: Could be kernel selection + different compilation options for attention. We picked kernels optimized for average seq length. For long contexts we can switch to a variant with different kernel/backing memory layouts; it's a quick config change and we should re-run that test.
[05:24] Speaker 1: (unlabeled) sorry interjection are there any limits on the KV cache size?
[05:30] Carlos: Max cache depends on node memory; we can provision larger KV per node in Dedicated. For Hosted there's shared limits but caching still helps.
[05:40] Priya: Network overhead what's the added latency for VPC peering? We need to ensure it doesn't blow the p95.
[05:47] Maya: Typically peering adds single-digit ms, but we'll run tests over the peered link. That's part of the 24h soak plan.
[05:55] Liam: Can you also produce a comparison table that calls out cost per 1M tokens for each config?
[06:02] Maya: Yes pricing worksheet will show Hosted vs Dedicated vs Dedicated+cache per-million-token unit economics, and we'll highlight pilot pricing.
[06:11] Jared: Any security gaps vs baseline? They advertise SOC two and bring-your-own-keys.
[06:18] Maya: We have SOC2, and BYOK via KMS/HSM we'll share the KMS integration doc. Audit logs are available with retention add-on.
[06:28] Priya: For the action items, can Carlos include raw p95/p99 histograms and the exact request distributions used?
[06:35] Carlos: Yup, raw histograms and the seed traffic generator configs are in the shared CSV. I'll include the exact load profile.
[06:43] Jared: Quick note when you talk about batching, we need to ensure product-side latency SLO is met; our PM will sign off only if p95 stays under 200ms on the sync route.
[06:55] Liam: Exactly that's the business criteria.
[07:00] Carlos: Noted we'll focus on p95 under 200ms in the next run, with caching enabled and tuned batching.
[07:07] Maya: Ok recap: Carlos rerun tests (batch sizes 1,4,8), include long-context kernel variant, run 24h soak on Dedicated with KV caching, Maya will send pricing and security docs, Priya to provide VPC config and traces.
[07:25] Priya: We'll send traces by Friday.
[07:28] Jared: Thanks team.
[07:30] Maya: Thanks everyone we'll follow up in email with links and next steps.
[07:35] (call ends)
